selection_criteria.reporting_period: Federal fiscal year 2025–26 (April 1, 2025 – March 31, 2026): the four disclosure quarters 2025-2026-Q1 … Q4. Complete: 90,759 source rows, matching the source's own quarterly totals exactly.
selection_criteria.value_ranked: contract_value = the disclosed TOTAL value of the contract (original plus amendments). It is a text column, so values are parsed to numbers and ranked locally (a server-side sort would be lexicographic). Rows with blank, zero or negative value are excluded (801 rows).
selection_criteria.what_counts_as_one_contract: procurement_id + normalized vendor name + owner department. reference_number is NOT used: it is unique per disclosure row (it embeds the quarter), so a contract re-reported for each amendment has many of them. A second pass collapses the same contract re-keyed within a department (vendor + department + original value + award date + delivery date).
selection_criteria.which_disclosure_is_used: The MOST RECENT disclosure of each contract (latest reporting period, then latest source row id). Not the maximum: cumulative values are not monotonic across amendments (e.g. one IBM contract: 804.0M, 798.8M, 797.8M, 796.2M in sequence).
selection_criteria.department_handling: A procurement disclosed by two departments is kept as two entries, because each department reports its own portion with its own original/amended values (verified on the Vancouver Shipyards contracts: 162.8M vs 13.7M original).
selection_criteria.tie_break: larger value first, then more recent disclosure
selection_criteria.not_represented_as: all Canadian federal contracts, or contracts awarded in the fiscal year. Amounts are total multi-year values and many contracts were awarded years earlier (award dates in the selection range from 1999 to 2026); they are in the selection because they were disclosed in this fiscal year.

result.label_shown_to_users: 100 largest federal contracts disclosed in fiscal year 2025–26
result.data_quality_note: Naive top-100 (sorted by value, no de-duplication) would have contained repeated entries for the same contract: in the top 30 alone, Parsons Inc. held 5 slots and Cascade Aerospace 3. After de-duplication each contract appears once.

firestore_read_strategy.document_ids: ca-fed-contract-001 … ca-fed-contract-100 (zero-padded rank, so id order = rank order). Fixed ids: a refresh overwrites the same 100 documents and cannot leave a stale tail.
firestore_read_strategy.query: where(documentId() >= 'ca-fed-contract-001') + where(documentId() <= 'ca-fed-contract-999') + orderBy(documentId()) + limit(20) [+ startAfter(last snapshot) for later pages]
firestore_read_strategy.index_and_rules: Uses Firestore's built-in __name__ index: NO composite index and NO rules change (government_contracts is already `allow read: if true`). The query shape was constructed with the real SDK offline to confirm it is valid.
firestore_read_strategy.reads_per_visit: Opening the Contracts page: 20 document reads. Each "Load 20 more": 20 reads. Full list: 5 pages = 100 reads, and only if the visitor asks for them; the last page does not trigger an extra empty read.
firestore_read_strategy.hub_screen: The Canada hub no longer prefetches contracts at all (it used to read every CA document just to show a count). The tile now reads "Largest federal contracts" with no count claim. US/UK/AU prefetch behaviour is unchanged.
firestore_read_strategy.aggregates: The combined value, selection size, fiscal year and basis are denormalized onto every document as selection_* fields, so the first page already carries them and no extra read is needed. They are the sum of exactly the 100 stored documents (checked by test).
firestore_read_strategy.active_completed: Derived at view time from end_date (the source delivery date), never stored, so it cannot go stale.
firestore_read_strategy.search_and_filters: Apply only to contracts loaded so far; the UI says so, and offers Load more.

sibling_engine_interaction.finding: The sibling civic-voice-engine repo already writes Canadian contracts into government_contracts, and its uploader deletes any document whose jurisdiction it uploads but which is not in its new upload set.
evidence: civic-voice-engine/src/ingestion/governmentContractsFetcher.js: fetchCanadaContracts() takes the top 500 by value from 10 recent periods, de-duplicated by reference_number, ids "CA-<reference_number>", jurisdiction "CA", status computed at fetch time. (Same reference_number flaw this MVP fixes: that key is unique per disclosure row, not per contract.)

civic-voice-engine/src/firebase/uploader.js uploadGovernmentContracts(): for each jurisdiction present in the upload it queries where('jurisdiction','==',jur) and DELETES every document whose id is not in the new upload. Run by the monthly scheduler (steps 11-12).

civic-voice-engine/functions/index.js aggregateContractStats (weekly): reads the WHOLE government_contracts collection and buckets totals into summary_stats/contract_stats by the `jurisdiction` field.
sibling_engine_interaction.risk_if_unaddressed: With jurisdiction "CA" the 100 selection documents would have been deleted as "stale" by the next monthly engine run (the page would silently go empty) and blended into the legacy Canadian totals.
sibling_engine_interaction.fix_applied: Selection documents use jurisdiction "CA-FED-SELECTION". The Contracts page pages by document id and never filters on jurisdiction, so the UI is unaffected. A test asserts the value is not one of the engine's CA/US/UK/AU, and (when the sibling repo is present) that its cleanup is still keyed on the jurisdiction field.
sibling_engine_interaction.id_collision: None possible: engine ids are "CA-C-…" (uppercase, sanitised); ours are lowercase "ca-fed-contract-NNN" and the page range is ca-fed-contract-001..999.
sibling_engine_interaction.decision_needed: The engine will keep writing its ~500 legacy "CA" documents every month. The Contracts page no longer reads them. Whether to retire the engine's Canada contracts fetch (a change in the OTHER repo) is a separate decision; nothing in either repo was changed or deleted.

statements_on_the_page: Disclosed in FY 2025–26: the contracts appear in the government's contract disclosures for April 1, 2025 – March 31, 2026; many were awarded earlier.
Values can cover multiple years: each amount is the contract's total reported value over its whole term, not one year's payments.
Values include reported amendments: original value plus any amendments reported to date.
A selected subset: the 100 largest by that value, not every federal contract.
Not federal spending: the combined value adds up reported contract values; it is not what the government spent during FY 2025–26. The combined-value tile carries the same caption.
